guion_largo.texto:
A ramp is a sloping path, without steps. This one has something special: it is made of slabs with engraved animals.

According to the INAH guide, it has two hundred seventy slabs. México Desconocido counts two hundred fifty-five. Medina Romero speaks of two hundred seventy-one, out of a total of more than four hundred engraved slabs found at the site. The figures do not agree. That is why here we say: more than two hundred fifty.

Medina Romero adds that many of the engraved species still exist. In other words, those who carved them looked at their surroundings and drew them in stone. Kenneth Hirth, on the other hand, speaks of mythical animals. Both descriptions can be true at the same time: a ramp with real fauna and imagined fauna.

INAH Lugares explains that the ramp connects with the ballcourt to the east. That suggests that the game and the ramp were part of the same complex.

The animal remains from the city tell something similar. According to Eduardo Corona, jaguar, peccary, bobcat and river crocodile appear mostly in the upper areas, almost always turned into ornaments or offerings. Deer, dog and puma appear at every level. In the lower part there are catfish, ducks, turtles and otters.

Look for an animal you know and another that does not look familiar. Think that someone chose which animals to place and in what order.

texto.pregunta: Myth: All the animals on the ramp are mythical.
